$comment: The weighted contract for lmms_video_tutorial. REVISED after the first trial.
SHAPE. Named atomic checks with small weights, grouped in the recording's own order, so the
score reads as how far through the tutorial the agent got. That is the model the Blender
rigging rubric uses (FILES/RESOURCES/t19rig-cu-astra-v04-regrade-20260910/.../RUBRIC-v04.md).
WHAT THE FIRST TRIAL CHANGED. Sonnet 5 scored 0.1923 while having correctly identified and
loaded AnalogBell, Muffled Bells, BinaryPiano1 and GhostBoy, found the staged 808 pack, set the
tempo to 100, and added three effects. It earned almost nothing for any of it, because every
instrument check was gated behind a note count sized for a FINISHED thirty-bar arrangement: the
melody needed 60 notes and had 8, the hi-hat needed 100 and had 16. That is a false negative on
the exact skill this task exists to measure, so every instrument check is now split in two:
* instruments_loaded  - the right preset or sample is on a track with at least one note. This
is the identification skill, and it is worth 28% of the score on its own.
* instruments_filled  - the part is actually written out across the arrangement.
An agent that identifies everything and finishes nothing now lands near 0.44 rather than 0.19,
which is a fair description of what it did.
TWO OTHER FALSE NEGATIVES FIXED. The drum checks demanded exact stock filenames, so an 808
snare from the pack this package itself stages scored zero; they now accept any snare, any
hi-hat, and either a kick sample or LMMS's own Kicker instrument. And a check that rewarded
leaving LMMS's default empty track untouched has been deleted outright: the first trial reused
that track for its first instrument, which is a perfectly sensible thing to do, and lost points
for tidiness.
EFFECTS ARE NOW GRADED, and the earlier decision to exclude them was wrong twice over. The
stated reason was that the recording never applies any effects. It does: at about 15:30 a
caption reads 'ADDED REVERB, DELAY AND SOME EQ' and the frame shows a Calf Reverb LADSPA loaded
into a track's own effects chain. The remaining objection was that adding an effect had never
been verified as drivable by coordinate, and the first trial settled that for free by doing it:
three LADSPA effects on one track, two enabled. Any effect counts, because requiring the Calf
plugin by name would fail an agent that reached for the built-in ReverbSC instead.
WHAT IS STILL DELIBERATELY NOT GRADED, and why each would fail a compliant agent:
* TEMPO. The caption at 0:00 reads 'BPM-100 OR ANY OF YOUR CHOICE', so any tempo is licensed,
including the 140 LMMS starts with.
* EXACT PITCHES AND CHORDS. Improvised freehand on camera, never stated, and individual note
rows are not reliably readable at the source resolution.
* TIMBRE. The third-party packs are absent, so fixtures/samples ships synthesized stand-ins
under the same names. Nothing here compares sound, and nothing could: the agent receives
screenshots and never audio.
* THE FILENAME. Any saved project counts, following the rigging rubric's filename neutrality.
TRACK IDENTITY IS MATCHED ON NAME, tolerantly and case-insensitively, because the extractor has
no column for which preset was loaded and LMMS names a track after the preset it loads. Matching
is on a fragment ('%bell%', '%ghost%') because the recording's own Song Editor shows 'Muffed
Bells' for a preset filed as 'Muffled Bells'.
TWO CHECKS CATCH A MODEL THAT DID NOT WATCH: per-note panning on the hi-hat track, and the drum
break across bars 13 and 14. Both are arbitrary and unguessable from knowing what a trap beat
is. The break is counted over notes AND beat/bassline clips, because the first trial built its
drums in the Beat/Bassline editor while the recording builds them as instrument tracks, and both
are legitimate.
There are no protected invariants: this episode stages no project, so there is nothing to
preserve and protected_state is a constant 1.0.
initial_task_progress is 0.0 - the episode's LMMS is empty, so a trial that does nothing has
nothing to be credited for. Measured by tests/preflight.py, not assumed.

assertions.$note: 0:15 - the TripleOscillator AnalogBell preset, with at least one note in it. Low bar on purpose: identifying the preset off the screen is the skill, and the first trial got this right while scoring zero because every check was gated behind a finished arrangement.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'tripleoscillator' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%analogbell%' AND note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 1:45 - a ZynAddSubFX bell preset layered under the melody.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'zynaddsubfx' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%bell%' AND note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 3:15 - the second ZynAddSubFX preset, BinaryPiano1.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'zynaddsubfx' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%piano%' AND note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 13:30 - the GhostBoy preset, added late.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'tripleoscillator' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%ghost%' AND note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 3:45 - any snare sample. The recording uses stock snare03.ogg; an 808 snare from the staged pack is an equally sensible reading and the first trial was wrongly failed for choosing one.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks t JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(s.source_name) LIKE '%snare%') AND t.note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 4:30 - any hi-hat sample, stock or from the 808 pack.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks t JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(s.source_name) LIKE '%hihat%') AND t.note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 7:00 - a kick, either a kick sample or LMMS's own Kicker instrument. The first trial used Kicker, which is a fair substitute for a kick sample and was wrongly failed.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks t LEFT JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%kick%' OR t.instrument = 'kicker') AND t.note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 11:15 - a bass loaded into the SF2 Player from the soundfont pack.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'sf2player' AND note_count >= 1

assertions.$note: 14:45 - at least one vocal one-shot on its own track.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) FROM tracks t JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE LOWER(s.source) LIKE '%vocal chops%' OR LOWER(s.source_name) LIKE '%cymatics%'

assertions.$note: The melody actually written out across the arrangement rather than sketched for a bar or two.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'tripleoscillator' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%analogbell%' AND note_count >= 40

assertions.$note: The bell layer written out.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'zynaddsubfx' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%bell%' AND note_count >= 15

assertions.$note: The chord part written out.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'zynaddsubfx' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%piano%' AND note_count >= 15

assertions.$note: The late lead written out.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks WHERE instrument = 'tripleoscillator' AND LOWER(name) LIKE '%ghost%' AND note_count >= 15

assertions.$note: A snare pattern rather than a couple of hits.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks t JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(s.source_name) LIKE '%snare%') AND t.note_count >= 20

assertions.$note: The hi-hat is the densest part of the recording, with 1/16 and 1/32 rolls, so this floor is the highest of the set.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks t JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(s.source_name) LIKE '%hihat%') AND t.note_count >= 60

assertions.$note: A kick pattern across the arrangement.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM tracks t LEFT JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%kick%' OR t.instrument = 'kicker') AND t.note_count >= 20

assertions.$note: Both vocal one-shots, as the recording ends up with.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) FROM tracks t JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE LOWER(s.source) LIKE '%vocal chops%' OR LOWER(s.source_name) LIKE '%cymatics%'

assertions.$note: 9:00 - WATCH-DISCRIMINATOR. Panning set one note at a time in the piano roll's Note Panning lane. Nothing about a trap beat implies it; only someone who watched would do it.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notes n JOIN tracks t ON t.id = n.track_id JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE LOWER(s.source_name) LIKE '%hihat%' AND n.pan <> 0

assertions.$note: WATCH-DISCRIMINATOR. The drums drop out for bars 13 and 14 and come back. Counted over both representations, because building drums as instrument tracks and building them in the Beat/Bassline editor are both legitimate and the first trial chose the latter. Both halves are required, so a project that merely stops before bar 13 cannot pass.
assertions.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notes n JOIN tracks t ON t.id = n.track_id LEFT JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%hihat%' OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%snare%' OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%kick%' OR t.instrument = 'kicker') AND (n.song_pos_ticks / 192) IN (12, 13)) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bb_clips c WHERE c.pos_ticks < 2688 AND (c.pos_ticks + COALESCE(c.len_ticks, 0)) > 2304)) = 0 AND ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notes n JOIN tracks t ON t.id = n.track_id LEFT JOIN samples s ON s.track_id = t.id WHERE (LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%hihat%' OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%snare%' OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.source_name,'')) LIKE '%kick%' OR t.instrument = 'kicker') AND (n.song_pos_ticks / 192) >= 14) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bb_clips c WHERE c.pos_ticks >= 2688)) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END

assertions.$note: 15:30 - the caption reads 'ADDED REVERB, DELAY AND SOME EQ' and the frame shows a reverb loaded into a track's own effects chain. Any effect counts: requiring the Calf plugin the recording happens to use would fail an agent that reached for LMMS's built-in ReverbSC, which does the same job.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM effects WHERE owner_kind = 'track' AND enabled = 1

assertions.$note: The caption names three things, so three is the full mark. Graded separately from the first so adding one reverb still earns something.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM effects WHERE owner_kind = 'track'

assertions.$note: The finished Song Editor holds eleven tracks. Nine is the floor so a reproduction missing a couple still scores.
assertions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tracks WHERE parent_track_id IS NULL

assertions.$note: 15:45 - the arrangement is spread out to about bar 30. 5184 ticks is bar 27, leaving room for a reproduction a few bars short. The first trial reached 576, which is bar 3. Graded as a floor, not an equality: the arrangement only has to REACH bar 27.
assertions.sql: SELECT length_ticks FROM project WHERE id = 1

assertions.$note: Any saved project under any name, following the rigging rubric's filename neutrality.
assertions.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN LOWER(value) LIKE '%.mmp' OR LOWER(value) LIKE '%.mmpz' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM state_meta WHERE key = 'source_name'

assertions.$note: Container and codec are checked as well as the extension, so another format renamed .wav does not pass. The instruction asks for this; the recording never exports.
assertions.sql: SELECT MIN(COUNT(*), 1) FROM renders WHERE probed = 1 AND path LIKE '/home/agent/Music/%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.wav' AND sample_rate = 44100 AND channels = 2 AND container LIKE '%wav%' AND codec LIKE 'pcm%'

assertions.$note: The first trial exported a file of the right format and length whose every sample was zero, and reported success. No ffprobe field distinguishes that from a real render; peak amplitude is the only one that can. Full scale for 16-bit is near 32767. Weighted at 6 rather than 3 because a silent export is a failed delivery rather than a blemish: the client receives nothing usable. At weight 3 a run that built the whole track and shipped silence still scored 0.95.
assertions.sql: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(peak_amplitude), 0) FROM renders WHERE probed = 1 AND path LIKE '/home/agent/Music/%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.wav' AND sample_rate = 44100 AND channels = 2 AND container LIKE '%wav%' AND codec LIKE 'pcm%'

assertions.$note: Thirty bars is 72s at 100bpm and 51s at 140. The 30s floor rules out an export truncated to a few bars without grading tempo through the back door. The first trial exported 9.6s.
assertions.sql: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(duration_ms), 0) FROM renders WHERE probed = 1 AND path LIKE '/home/agent/Music/%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.wav' AND sample_rate = 44100 AND channels = 2 AND container LIKE '%wav%' AND codec LIKE 'pcm%'
